title: Interim capacity hedge for midcycle feature snapdowns (pilot)
creator: Sofia Delgado
description: Problem: sudden midcycle scope snapdowns (urgent scope cuts, unplanned customer requests, and incident-driven work) have repeatedly forced downstream de-scopes and cross-team fire drills. We lack a small, repeatable mechanism teams can opt into to absorb ~10-25% unexpected load without derailing committed OKRs. This ticket defines a lightweight interim capacity hedge pilot that converts a predictable micro-allocation of effort into a transparent, tradeable buffer that teams can draw against during the cycle.
background: Observed: over the past 6 cycles ~18% of feature work was impacted by unplanned follow-on tasks (support escalations, infra incidents, urgent security patches), with variance concentrated in midcycle weeks.
Existing mitigations (on-call, ad-hoc re-prioritization) are inconsistent and create cross-team churn.
Goal: reduce destructive midcycle re-scopes and increase predictability for product commitments while keeping the mechanism light and reversible.
proposed_solution: Introduce a 3-tier Capacity Hedge (Green/Amber/Red) allocated at the initiative level at cycle start. Hedge is expressed as 'surge tokens' (headcount-hours) assigned to initiatives and managed by PM + tech lead.

Tier definitions: Green = up to 8% of planned sprint effort (routine small follow-ups), Amber = additional 10% (moderate emergent work), Red = contingency reserve (extra 10–12%) held centrally for critical mitigation.

Operational model: teams opt-in to use their Green/Amber tokens autonomously with a short post-incident blameless writeup. Use of Amber requires cross-functional approval from the initiative lead and product operations. Red draws are escalated to the cycle steward (PM director) and require an explicit reforecast of scope.

Accounting: convert surge tokens into 'developer-days' and show real-time burn in the cycle dashboard. Tokens not used roll into the next cycle as a limited one-time credit (half-life carryover of 50% of unused Green tokens).
Pilot length: one cycle (2026-W12) with 6 engineering teams participating; success criteria collected via metrics and team surveys.
acceptance_criteria: Pilot policy documented in Confluence with step-by-step draw process and approval matrix.
Dashboard tile in Console-metrics showing hedge allocation, burn, and remaining tokens per initiative.
Participation agreement signed by 6 teams and their engineering leads before cycle start.
Observed reduction in forced OKR de-scope events for participating teams versus matched control group during the pilot cycle.
Post-cycle retrospective with recommended improvements and decision to expand / sunset the policy.
risks_and_tradeoffs: Risk of moral hazard: teams may over-commit believing buffer exists — mitigated by limiting Green to low-percent and requiring writeups for draws.
Administrative overhead: tracking tokens and approvals adds process; pilot reduces scope by using a minimal approval matrix and automated dashboard alerts.
Carryover complexity: half-life credit adds bookkeeping; limit to a single-cycle credit to reduce long-term accrual.
metrics: Primary: percent of midcycle forced de-scopes for pilot teams (target: reduce by 40% relative to prior 3-cycle baseline).
Secondary: unplanned work ratio (unplanned story points / total committed points) during week 3–6 of cycle; target < 15%.
Operational: average time-to-approval for Amber draws (goal: < 24 hours), Red draw response SLA (goal: < 48 hours).
Qualitative: team satisfaction score from end-of-cycle survey (goal: +0.5 improvement on 5-point scale).

Instrument Console dashboard with hedge widgets (owner: metrics eng) — PR: github.com/redwood/console/pull/4721.
Create a small UI flow in the initiative sidebar for teams to request Amber/Red draws (owner: product eng).
Pilot kickoff slack channel and weekly 15-min sync for participating leads.
Retrospective and final recommendation doc due 2026-04-05.
rollout_plan: Pilot (2026-W12): 6 teams opt in, limited to 3 months of data collection.
Evaluation: PM Ops will review metrics and qualitative feedback; publish recommendation for expansion by 2026-04-10.
If approved: turn policy into a templated initiative line-item, add automated token accounting, and expand to all Platform & Core product teams in the following cycle.
test_plan: Simulate two common midcycle events in a tabletop exercise (incident patch and urgent customer feature tweak) and validate draw workflow and dashboard visibility.
End-of-cycle A/B comparison with matched non-participating teams on de-scope frequency and delivery variance.
Spot audit of draws for documentation quality and adherence to approval rules.

notes_and_outcomes_expected: Short term: fewer ad-hoc cross-team re-prioritizations and clearer visible accounting of unplanned work.
Long term: if pilot succeeds, incorporate capacity hedges into standard cycle planning templates and automate token flows in Console.
If pilot fails: document failure modes (moral hazard / overhead) and consider alternative mitigations (hard reserve lanes or stronger pre-cycle freeze on scope changes).
